answer: Sybil farms can hide one operator behind many keys whose answers all lean toward the same horizon of near-copies. Use a public commit-reveal trellis of walnut tickets: each new key must post a unique ticket on two earlier rungs with staggered timestamps before its answer counts, and tickets that later cluster with a known farm are voided. The cost is slower first credit and more setup work for honest thin keys. Verification is the on-chain ticket map plus cluster judgments at close. It fails if a wealthy farm pre-grows a clean trellis and treats voided walnut tickets as a routine fee.
